newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banks group-ECB should target money supply.
newsitem.headline: German banks group-ECB should target money supply.

text.p: The future European Central Bank (ECB) should use money supply rather than inflation targets to guide its monetary policy, the Federation of German Cooperative Banks (BVR) said on Thursday.

The BVR said that while the time-lag between an interest rate move and its impact on inflation was long, the lag with money supply was significantly shorter, making it easier to judge the effectiveness of monetary policy.

The relationship between money supply and price developments in a large currency would be more stable than data currently show for Germany, and in adopting money supply targets, the ECB could associate itself with the stability-orientated policies of the Bundesbank, the BVR said in a report.

The European Monetary Institute (EMI), which will be succeeded by the ECB in 1998, has suggested interest rates should be set in relation to either money supply or inflation targets, but has left it up to the ECB itself to make the final decision.

Money supply targeting is the method favoured by the Bundesbank, but many European central banks have abandoned the indicator as a monetary tool because of distortions and fluctuations in the data in recent years.
The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said earlier this month that a direct inflation target would be more reliable as an ECB policy guide.
